---
title: "Errors and warnings"
description: "Catch package-origin errors and filter warnings by class."
execute:
  eval: false
---

Use condition classes to handle failures selectively. The text of an error is
for readers; the package does not require callers to match that text.

```python
from metasalmonpy import MetasalmonValidationError
from metasalmonpy.sdp_schema import set_sdp_schema_source

try:
    set_sdp_schema_source("unknown")
except MetasalmonValidationError as error:
    print(error)  # Report the schema setting that needs correction.
```

## Catch surfaces

`MetasalmonCondition` is the common base. `MetasalmonError` covers errors
explicitly constructed by this package, and `MetasalmonWarning` covers warnings
explicitly emitted by it. The warning base does not inherit from the error base.

| Family | Error | Warning | Scope |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Validation | `MetasalmonValidationError` | `MetasalmonValidationWarning` | Dictionary/schema checks, SDP extension and semantic-file contracts, SSSOM, observation/measurement structures and reproducibility manifests. |
| LLM | `MetasalmonLlmError` | `MetasalmonLlmWarning` | Model-review adapters and chat decomposition, including their context-file checks. |
| Publication | `MetasalmonPublicationError` | `MetasalmonPublicationWarning` | KNB/DataONE, EML, EDH, Darwin Core export and GitHub access. |
| Retrieval | `MetasalmonRetrievalError` | `MetasalmonRetrievalWarning` | Vocabulary/ontology fetching, including ICES. |

These families follow the responsible module. Other modules expose the common
package error/warning bases. For example, package assembly and structural
validation in `package_io` use `MetasalmonError`; the structural validation error
still carries its complete `.issues` frame. A function's name alone does not
determine its family.

All public bases above are available from `metasalmonpy` and
`metasalmonpy.conditions`. Concrete implementation subclasses are private.

## Existing handlers and filters

Every package emission retains its original builtin exception or warning type.
A schema-setting error remains a `ValueError`; invalid context objects remain
`TypeError`; missing files remain `FileNotFoundError`. Existing
`except ValueError` and `except OSError` handlers continue to work.

`SdpSchemaError`, `SdpExtensionError`, `ReproducibilityManifestError` and
`KnbHttpError` keep their existing names, constructors and metadata. The HTTP
error's `.status` remains available. Messages, `args`, OSError path/errno
attributes and exception causes remain intact.

Warning filters also retain their previous builtin categories:

```python
import warnings
from metasalmonpy import MetasalmonRetrievalWarning

with warnings.catch_warnings():
    warnings.simplefilter("error", MetasalmonRetrievalWarning)
    # Run your vocabulary lookup here. Package retrieval warnings now raise.
```

An existing filter for `RuntimeWarning`, `UserWarning` or `DeprecationWarning`
still matches the corresponding derived package warning. Converting warnings
to errors can expose an incomplete retrieval as a failed lookup; handle that
according to your workflow rather than interpreting it as an ontology gap.

## Dependency failures

Exceptions from a dependency, the operating system or an injected callback
keep their original identity and type when propagated. Optional/core dependency
`ImportError` guards and YAML loader `ConstructorError` diagnostics retain their
existing dependency-specific types. The hierarchy describes package emissions;
it does not recategorize every error raised during a package call.

No ontology term is selected or approved by catching a condition.
